tier_reason: The colfer row in the independent alecthomas/go_serialization_benchmarks report (1.6k stars) shows 115/123 ns/op, against 287/356 ns/op for the official protobuf-go row. The code is public (benchmarks.go, internal/serializers/colfer), but the report says it is 'user-generated' and gives no CPU model or Go version, so it cannot be A.

corrections.caveats: The report page (report/data.js, rendered at alecthomas.github.io/go_serialization_benchmarks, last fully regenerated 2025-07-04 in commit 833ed64) says 'This report is user-generated'. The numbers come from a contributor's local run, not CI (CI only runs --validate). No CPU model or Go version is given, so the tier is capped at B. Numbers cover one struct shape only. The win is against official protobuf-go (google.golang.org/protobuf v1.34.2). Against the codegen gogo/protobuf row on the same page, Colfer ties on marshal (115 vs 115 ns/op) and is ~1.35x faster on unmarshal (123 vs 166 ns/op) (derived from page data). Colfer's own wiki benchmark agrees (Apple M1, go1.20.2, vs gogo/protobuf 1.3.2): marshal 35.08 vs 34.89 ns/op, unmarshal 44.85 vs 60.01 ns/op. CC0-1.0 public-domain dedication: no patent grant.

notes: All claimed numbers match the colfer, protobuf-go, msgpack and capnproto rows. Metadata checks out: CC0-1.0, 759 stars, last commit 2026-02-26, active, not archived or a fork. For the C++-first list: the Colfer wiki also has a first-party C benchmark against protobuf C++ (c/bench/bench.cpp, -O3 in c/bench/Makefile, Apple clang 15.0.0, Apple M1, libprotoc 24.4). It gives marshal 9.19 vs 22.9 ns and unmarshal 18.0 vs 40.8 ns and could support a separate C entry at tier A.

tier_reason: In the same independent go_serialization_benchmarks report, the gencode rows (122/132 ns/op; unsafe_reuse 48/104) sit next to the protobuf-go row (287/356 ns/op). The code is public, but the report is user-generated with no CPU model or Go version, so it cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Safe variant: marshal 122 ns/op vs protobuf-go 287 ns/op (~2.35x), unmarshal 132 vs 356 ns/op (~2.7x). gencode/unsafe_reuse variant (buffer reuse plus unsafe strings; protobuf-go has no like-for-like row): marshal 48 ns/op (~6x), unmarshal 104 ns/op (~3.4x) (derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: The shared report page is user-generated (the page says so; CI only validates, last regenerated 2025-07-04) and gives no CPU model or Go version, so the tier is capped at B. The ~6x marshal figure compares the unsafe_reuse variant with a protobuf-go row that does not reuse buffers, so it is not like-for-like. Against gogo/protobuf on the same page, gencode is slightly slower on marshal (122 vs 115 ns/op) and faster on unmarshal (132 vs 166 ns/op). The shootout uses checked-in generated gencode code; its Makefile generator lines are commented out. GPL-2.0 is copyleft. Unmaintained, last commit 2017-11-24, but still useful as a technique reference.

notes: The numbers match the page. The 2.3-6x range was clarified so the ~6x upper bound is tied to the unsafe_reuse variant. last_commit corrected: 2018-08-13 is the repo's pushed_at date, and the latest commit on master (the only branch) is 2017-11-24. The license (GPL-2.0), 324 stars and abandoned status are correct. The README's own benchmark compares only against GOB, JSON and MSGP, not protobuf.

tier_reason: The independent go_serialization_benchmarks report shows the msgp row at 134/200 ns/op and 97 B, against the vmihailenco/msgpack row (the incumbent reflection-based Go MessagePack library) at 921/1216 ns/op and 92 B. The code is public, but the report is user-generated with no CPU model or Go version, so it cannot be A.

corrections.caveats: msgp and vmihailenco/msgpack are both MessagePack implementations, so the win is codegen vs reflection over the same wire format, not a new format. The shared report page is user-generated (the page says so; CI only validates, last regenerated 2025-07-04) and gives no CPU model or Go version, so the tier is capped at B. The shootout pins msgp v1.1.8 and vmihailenco/msgpack v5.3.5, while the current msgp release is v1.6.4. Against the other codegen MessagePack entry (shamaton/msgpackgen/map, 242/358 ns/op), msgp is ~1.8x faster (derived from page data).

notes: All claimed numbers and sizes match the msgp and msgpack rows, and the ratios (~6.9x, ~6.1x) are correct. Metadata checks out: MIT, 1,951 stars, last commit 2026-09-21, active, not archived or a fork.
